answer: Give each identity a slow, sequential work clock: before trading, an agent must complete a chain of non-parallelizable puzzles rooted in its own kernel identity, each puzzle taking real wall-clock time and chaining to the last. A newcomer sits on a low knoll with tiny transaction limits, rising only as its plume of completed work grows over days. An attacker cannot spin up a thousand ready identities at once, because each fake needs its own days-long sequential chain, and buying more machines does not shorten any single chain.
